source: kaggriculture-episodes-analyses: per-game-day tables; the rival axis comes from offline_lab/build/realised_supply.py, which solves the city inventory identity (inv_g(t) - inv_g(t-1) = our_sells + their_sells - drain_g) in DuckDB

arrays.rival_supply: float32 (W, 31, 9) units their harvesting puts on the market, by day
arrays.demand: float32 (W, 31, 9) the town's appetite, by day
arrays.weights: float32 (W,) share of the archive each world stands for, sums to 1.0
arrays.crop: <U10 (9,) the good order every array uses
arrays.phase0/phase1: int8 (W,) the day window the world was cut from (0-9 / 10-14 / 15+)
arrays.support: int32 (W,) game-days behind the world: its evidence

prices: deliberately NOT stored: a world becomes prices only through the agent's own _priced_paths, so there is one definition of a price path, not two
measured: realised/logged supply runs 25% (WHEAT, the shed caps hardest) to 83% (STRAWBERRY) over 829 games; orders are not sales

timing_weights.keyed_by: agent identity, both seats pooled -- never by seat index
timing_weights.pool: win rate >= 60% over >= 30 games, measured on the ten newest partitions (4 agents; a 70% cut leaves a single agent and a 159-game agent looked strong at 79% in one partition but is 57% over its 1342 games -- the label must come from volume)

contrast_weak_half.definition: agents below 50% win rate, same partitions
contrast_weak_half.direction: slower in all five crops, so the signal is real, not noise

timing_weights.open: the supply axis in this file is still seat-based; keying it by agent identity needs the inventory identity solved per partition and then filtered by the same pool
